sentences.text:
The applicant No.1 Sarpu is in custody from 27.12.2023,
applicant No.2 Ajay is in custody since 10.2.2024 and applicant No.3 Sangita Bai is in custody from 11.03.2024.
2. Allegations against the applicants are of abduction of the prosecutrix and commission of rape upon the minor prosecutrix.
3. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that applicants are innocent and they have falsely been implicated in the case.
The prosecutrix went to Gujrat and resided with the applicant by her own wish.
No objection has also been filed by the parents of the prosecutrix regarding grant of bail.
In support of the same, they have filed an affidavit regarding the same.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicants be released on bail, pending the trial.
4.Learned counsel for the objector has expressed his no objection regarding the bail application.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

6. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, custody period of the applicant, trial of the case will take considerable time, I am inclined to release the applicants on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicants, stands allowed.

7. It is directed that applicants be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for their regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that they shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

They shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PREM NARAYAN SINGH) JUDGE VD Sarpu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27746744/
